clue.text: Cleaning agent excessively used, in the old days

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too much

indicators.note: the word in tells us the old days sit inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written
the old days are the past

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a household cleaner was used far too much in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' does no work beyond joining; the comma tempts you to read 'excessively used' as a single idea, but only 'excessively' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the paste you brush onto your teeth to clean them, so it is a cleaning product.

clue.text: Musical old organ

parts.note: the liver is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: An antique organ is played in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a church instrument; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Bart's stage show based on Dickens is a famous musical.

clue.text: Wearing tie, try to rise in company

indicators.note: something wearing an item has it around it, so the word for tie goes round the other piece

parts.note: to tether is to tie up

indicators.note: in a down clue, to rise means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a tie tries to stand up at a business gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' reverses the word for try (making OG), and 'Wearing' puts that reversal inside the word for tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with others, in one another's company, is being jointly.

clue.text: Innocent was, at various times, so dogmatic

definitions.text: Innocent was, at various times, so
definitions.meaning: Innocent was the name of thirteen popes, so at various times he was papal
pompously laying down the law, as a pope might

explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent' looks like an adjective; it is the papal name.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a pope, and by extension pompously authoritative or dogmatic.

clue.text: Vivid colour of a detective's study …

definitions.meaning: A Study in ... is the first Sherlock Holmes story, so the study is of this

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue, which also turns on Holmes, whose rooms were in Baker Street.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bright red hue, and the colour in the title of Conan Doyle's first Holmes story.

clue.text: … formerly in Baker Street

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words Baker Street

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes was once in Baker Street.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word meaning once, at an earlier time, as in erstwhile.

clue.text: Ruffian spilt oil in log hut

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the hut

parts.note: a hogan is a Navajo log and earth dwelling

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: A thug knocked over oil inside a log cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' rearranges OIL into OLI, put 'in' HOGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent young troublemaker is a thug or ruffian.

clue.text: Linger in seedy resort, out of touch with reality

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other
resort, read as re-sort, means the letters are sorted again

parts.note: to tarry is to linger

explanation.surface: Someone lingers in a run-down seaside resort, losing their grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a holiday town but is re-sort, rearranging the letters of seedy as SEYED around the word for linger.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dreamily idealistic and naive is out of touch with reality.

clue.text: Bring word about place of refuge

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a port is a harbour, a place where ships take refuge

explanation.surface: A messenger brings news concerning a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring word of something is to give an account of it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Lass seen around Richmond

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, so it can stand for a lass
Richmond is the capital of the US state, so the state is seen all around it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Richmond' suggests the London suburb or the Yorkshire town; here it is the state capital in America.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a girl's name and the US state whose capital is Richmond.

clue.text: Tradesman providing useful service for victims of farmer's wife?

definitions.text: Tradesman providing useful service for victims of farmer's wife?

parts.words: Tradesman providing useful service for victims of farmer's wife?
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off the tails of three blind mice, so the mice would want someone to put tails back on again

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper looks after customers who suffered at the hands of a farmer's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The victims are the Three Blind Mice of the nursery rhyme; read the answer as RE-TAILER, one who tails again.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling goods to the public is a seller of this kind, a tradesman.

clue.text: Affectedly roguish chief in combinations

definitions.meaning: playfully mischievous in a knowing, slightly superior way
as a prefix in compound words it means chief, as in archbishop or archenemy

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means coyly mischievous, and the prefix means principal, as in archbishop.

clue.text: One of the characters found in (Saint) James

definitions.text: One of the characters found in (Saint) James

parts.words: One of the characters found in (Saint) James
parts.note: a diplomat is accredited to the Court of St James's in London, and the title figures in a Henry James novel, so this is a figure found in both

explanation.surface: A figure appears in a Henry James novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry James wrote The Ambassadors; foreign envoys to Britain are accredited to the Court of St James's.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior diplomat who represents a country abroad, as envoys do at the Court of St James's.

clue.text: Ships, one by one, abandoning Spithead for a brief period

parts.note: a fleet is a body of ships

indicators.note: abandoning tells us a letter is dropped from the word for one by one

parts.note: singly means one at a time, one by one
the head of Spit is its first letter, S; Spithead is also a naval anchorage off Portsmouth

explanation.surface: Ships leave the Spithead anchorage one after another for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: Spithead is a stretch of water off Portsmouth where the fleet anchors, but the clue wants the head of 'Spit', S, removed from SINGLY to leave INGLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done briefly or transiently happens only for a short moment.

clue.text: Theologians originally learnt about the old scriptures way back

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of Theologians
about tells us the word for learnt goes round the old word for the

parts.note: to have heard something is to have learnt it
ye is an old form of the
OT is the Old Testament, scriptures

explanation.surface: Theologians first learnt about ancient scriptures long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is the archaic spelling of 'the'; HEARD goes 'about' it to make HEYEARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for a time long ago, as in 'since the year dot'.

clue.text: Loudly criticise military accommodation

definitions.meaning: to jeer or shout down a performer or team, as sports crowds do
a building where soldiers are housed

explanation.walkthrough: Barracking a team, jeering at it, is everyday British and Australian sporting speech.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means jeer at noisily; as a noun it is a block housing soldiers.

clue.text: Thinking conservationists provide base for game bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, providing a base means coming at the bottom, after the rest

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
a mina, or myna, is a bird
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: Conservationists supply the foundation for a game bird's habitat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game bird' looks like one item but is two: RU and MINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows chew the cud, and a person deep in thought is said to chew things over, contemplating.

clue.text: Where waders are kept by woman employed on railway

parts.note: her is a word referring to a woman
on means working, employed, as in being on duty

explanation.surface: A woman working on the railway keeps a store of fishing boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waders' suggests anglers' boots; here they are wading birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony or breeding place of long-legged wading birds is where they live.

clue.text: Obtain food inside, being resident

indicators.note: inside tells us the food is placed within the other word

parts.note: to obtain is to prevail or exist, as in the rules that obtain, which is to occur
a pie is food

explanation.surface: Someone gets a meal indoors, living there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obtain' means get on the surface, but here it is the formal sense of being in existence.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living in a house is its tenant or inhabitant.

clue.text: European legislation, upsetting and silly

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns a word upside down, reversing it

parts.note: law is legislation
a loon is a silly person, a fool

explanation.surface: European laws are subversive and foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-speaking inhabitant of southern Belgium, so a European.

clue.text: This cooked makes start of Lent nice?

definitions.text: This cooked makes start of Lent nice?

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared afresh, rearranged
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Baking this treat makes the beginning of Lent pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges MAKES, L (the start of Lent) and NICE. The whole clue is the definition: this fruit cake is traditional in Lent, on Mothering Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich fruit cake topped with marzipan balls, traditionally baked in Britain for Mothering Sunday in mid-Lent or for Easter.

clue.text: Possibly a club eccentric

definitions.meaning: one suit of playing ... is clubs, so a club is an example of a playing ...
an odd or amusing person is often called this

explanation.definitionFit: A club is one example of a playing card, and an eccentric person is informally called this.

clue.text: Worship constantly during religious education

indicators.note: during places one piece within the other

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
ever means always, constantly

explanation.surface: People worship constantly in their scripture lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate or hold in deep respect is close to worship.

clue.text: Extraordinary woman hiding in a barrel

indicators.note: a woman hiding in something is placed inside it

parts.note: BL is the abbreviation for barrel
Norma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A remarkable woman is concealed inside a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusual or out of the ordinary deviates from the norm.

clue.text: Humble-sounding bearing

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for humble is spoken

parts.note: mean means lowly, humble, as in of mean birth

explanation.surface: A modest bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's demeanour or appearance is their bearing.

clue.text: Grandfather, possibly, or his clock?

definitions.meaning: a grandfather is likely to be an elderly man, a veteran
his clock is a grandfather clock, and a clock is a timer, an old one at that

explanation.definitionFit: An elderly man is a veteran, and an antique clock is an aged timepiece.

clue.text: A teacher initially in French department is kept busy

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces go inside the department

parts.note: the Orne is a department of Normandy in France

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of teacher

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher working in a French department is kept fully occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' reads as occupied, but it is the sense of over-elaborate decoration; 'is kept' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A design that is fussy and over-decorated is called busy, which is what elaborate ornamentation means.

clue.text: One not jumping who's unlikely to succeed?

definitions.meaning: a horse that does not start a race, so never jumps a fence
a person or plan with no chance of success

explanation.definitionFit: A horse withdrawn before the off never runs, and so a hopeless person or idea is called one too.
